items.title: Chester Jones Interview, 1961-07-10
items.q: The only time I was away from here, Bill, when I was with Artie Crossley's band, I went to Los Angeles and played out there.

ctx.x: Frog and I were talking about some of the things that make New Orleans music different than other things. Like he mentioned the melody and the fact that they get together, play together and a few other things as well. Another thing, as he said, his father told him about to be able to play any type of music. Is there anything, remarks you'd have about the particular kind of drumming that you've noticed? Any other drummers away from here that they're different than the fellows here, their beat or anything, if you…

Well no, I have never heard any of the guys playing all this music away from here. The only time I was away from here, Bill, when I was with Artie Crossley's band, I went to Los Angeles and played out there. Oh yeah. And in fact, we were the only band, they had the bandage to play there on Sundays, but I had never went down to here. So I couldn't say anything about the guys playing drums.

Have you ever had any experience of other drummers from outside of town coming in here and trying to play with some of your bands and noticed that they played differently or? No. Anything much about, different style or anything? No, I haven't. Is there anything that you can make any remarks about the New Orleans music? Things that you try to do with your drumming? What do you think the drums are your main job in the band? Like is it just keeping time or anything else that you could say is your job in the band?…
